defects.expected: one mode per sample (sampleStats.mode(i, :)) as for mean/median/std, matching the header

notes: Repro (MATLAB R2025a, after initCobraToolbox): m.rxns = {'r1';'r2'}; printSampleStats({[1 1 2; 3 4 4], [5 5 6; 7 8 8]}, m, {'A','B'}) -> rows have 7 values under 8 headings. Single-sample calls are correct. No toolbox caller (grep finds none). Also seen (not recorded as a defect, input outside the documented 'cell array of cell arrays' subSystems type although the field validator in COBRA_structure_fields.tab accepts char entries): m.subSystems = {'Glyc';'TCA'} stops at line 53 with 'First input must be a string array or cell array of character vectors.' (strjoin of a char).

defects.title: sparse(i, j, s) pairs the values with the sorted pattern, not with (i, j)
defects.trigger: raw = zeros(4, 2, 1, 'uint8'); raw(:, 1) = 10; raw(:, 2) = 20; vals = CMatrix(raw); f = full(sparse([2 1], [1 1], vals)); f.x(1, :)
defects.observed: bytes [10 20] at rows 1 and 2 while MATLAB's full(sparse([2 1], [1 1], [10 20]))' is [20 10]: the logical pattern (line 133) is column-major sorted but the values (135-136) keep input order; repeated pairs sparse([1 1], [1 1], vals) give a 1x1 object with 1 pattern nonzero and 2 stored values. No MEX involved.
defects.expected: S(i(k), j(k)) = s(k) as for MATLAB's sparse (repeated pairs summed or rejected)

notes: Repro (after initCobraToolbox, MATLAB R2025a): raw = zeros(4,2,1,'uint8'); raw(:,1) = 10; raw(:,2) = 20; vals = CMatrix(raw); f = full(sparse([2 1],[1 1],vals)); f.x(1,:) -> [10 20] (MATLAB: full(sparse([2 1],[1 1],[10 20]))' = [20 10]); r3 = sparse([1 1],[1 1],vals); r3.x -> nnz(r3.x{1}) = 1 but size(r3.x{2},2) = 2. The defect is confined to the call form sparse(i, j, s[, m, n[, nzmax]]) with an object of the class as an argument; no toolbox caller found uses that form (AdaptiveChol line 63 uses diag(sparse(w)), the 1-argument form), so no caller is blocked. CMatrix.m is the template that compileCMatrix copies to include/ddouble.m and include/qdouble.m (verified identical up to the class name); there is no C++ source for CMatrixMex itself, so CMatrix can never have its MEX. No MEX file exists for any of CMatrixMex/ddoubleMex/qdoubleMex (nor ARM variants); compileCMatrix needs the quarantined configCMatrix and writes into src/. Without MEX, about 1/3 of the lines can run (constructor from uint8/cell raw storage, size/length/numel/is*, end, '()' dense subsref/subsasgn, dense horzcat, reshape, full of sparse, sparse 3/5/6-arg with a class-object value, issparse, uplus, find with 3 outputs on sparse, assert errors of power/norm/mldivide/max) - a partial test was feasible had there been no defect. Side observation: in a function-argument context (disp(class(c.x))) the public property x fails with 'Too many output arguments' because the overloaded numel (6 for a 2x3 object) sets the output count of '.' indexing; c.x in an assignment works.
confirmed_by: lead (source read: the triplet constructor builds the pattern with sparse(i,j,...) and fills s in triplet order, lines 133-136, which differs from sparse's ordering for unsorted triplets)

defects.title: Mol files are missed when another file precedes them or their name holds a dot or 'mol'
defects.trigger: molfiledir holding A.txt, B.mol, C.mol, glc.D.mol, xmol.mol; getMetaboliteMsDistr({'B[c]'; 'C[c]'; 'glc.D[c]'; 'xmol[c]'}, molDir, outDir, [7 7.5])
defects.observed: with ispc and system replaced by recording stubs (MATLAB R2025a), only the call(s) for C are issued; B (preceded by A.txt in the concatenated listing '...A.txtB.molC.mol...'), glc.D (dots removed: 'glcD') and xmol (the unescaped '.' of '.mol' also matches 'xmol') get none (two calls for C, pH 7 and 7.5)
defects.expected: one cxcalc call per pH for every metabolite whose <id>.mol file exists

notes: Repro: a scratch folder with ispc.m (returns true) and system.m (appends cmd to getappdata(0,'probeSystemCalls')) added to the path (MATLAB warns that both shadow built-ins); molDir with empty files A.txt, B.mol, C.mol, glc.D.mol, xmol.mol; getMetaboliteMsDistr({'B[c]';'C[c]';'glc.D[c]';'xmol[c]'}, molDir, outDir, [7 7.5]) -> only 'cxcalc -o <out>/C_msdistr_ph7.sdf msdistr -H 7 -M true <mol>/C.mol' and the ph7.5 call. The cxcalc call only runs on Windows (ispc); on Linux the function only prints the indices, so apart from the defect a Linux test would be TESTED with the system line exempt (Windows-only + cxcalc not installed); the lead may prefer EXCLUDED instead of QUARANTINED since the defect is observable only through the Windows branch. No toolbox caller. Also: the paths are not quoted in the cxcalc command, so folders with spaces would break it (not recorded).
confirmed_by: lead (source read: regexp(..., '.mol', 'split') with an unescaped dot splits names that contain 'mol' anywhere; runs on every platform, lines 20-22)
